questions.question: Which property must a material possess for liquid particles to move through it via diffusion?
options: It must be impermeable
It must be permeable
It must be magnetic
It must be non-porous

questions.question: When observing a liquid diffusing into a jelly cube, what happens over time?
options: The liquid stays entirely on the outside surface
The liquid moves into the jelly cube gradually
The jelly cube instantly dissolves into gas
The liquid turns into a solid layer around the cube

questions.question: What effect does increasing the temperature have on the diffusion of a liquid into a jelly cube?
options: It speeds up the rate of diffusion
It slows down the rate of diffusion
It stops diffusion from happening
It has no effect on the rate of diffusion

questions.question: How does the size of a jelly cube affect the time it takes for a liquid to diffuse to its centre?
options: A smaller cube takes longer than a larger cube
A larger cube takes longer than a smaller cube
Cube size does not affect the time taken
Liquid can only diffuse into the largest cubes

questions.question: Using particle theory, why does diffusion occur faster at higher temperatures?
options: Particles gain kinetic energy and move faster
Particles become smaller and pass through faster
Particles stop colliding with one another
Particles join together to form large structures

questions.question: Which particles can diffuse through a selectively-permeable membrane?
options: Only particles that are large enough to fill the membrane
Only particles small enough to pass through the holes
All particles regardless of their size
No particles can pass through at all

questions.question: In what direction do particles move across a selectively-permeable membrane?
options: Only from the outside to the inside
In both directions across the membrane
Only from lower concentration to higher concentration
They do not move at all once inside

questions.question: If side X has a high concentration of small particles and side Y has a low concentration, what is the net movement?
options: Net movement from side Y to side X
Net movement from side X to side Y
Zero particle movement in either direction
Net movement alternates every second

questions.question: When observing Visking tubing containing starch and glucose placed in water, what net movement is observed?
options: Starch moves out of the tubing into the water
Glucose moves out of the tubing into the water
Both starch and glucose move out at the same rate
Water moves out but no dissolved substances move

questions.question: Why does glucose diffuse out of Visking tubing while starch remains inside?
options: Glucose particles are small enough to pass through the holes, but starch particles are too large
Glucose is liquid while starch is solid
Starch particles are destroyed by the tubing material
Glucose is pushed out by magnetic forces

questions.question: What are cell cytoplasm and the substances inside it made of?
options: Continuous fluids with no distinct structure
Particles
Air bubbles
Solid static crystals

questions.question: How do particles of some substances enter and leave a cell?
options: By passing through small holes in the cell membrane
By breaking down the cell membrane permanently
By turning into energy waves
By passing through the cell nucleus directly

questions.question: Why can some substances NOT diffuse through the cell membrane?
options: Their particles are too big to fit through the holes in the cell membrane
Their particles are too small to be noticed by the cell
They move too fast to enter the cell
They are repelled by the cell's cytoplasm

questions.question: Why is the cell membrane described as selectively-permeable?
options: It lets every substance pass through freely
It completely blocks all substances from entering
Only some substances can diffuse through its small holes
It only allows liquids to freeze on its surface

questions.question: What is the net movement of particles across a cell membrane?
options: Up a concentration gradient
Down a concentration gradient
Against a concentration gradient
In a fixed circular pattern

questions.question: How do particles behave as they diffuse in liquids or gases?
options: They move in straight lines without colliding
They move in random directions and collide continuously
They stay completely still until pushed
They move in a single organized direction

questions.question: What is the scientific definition of concentration?
options: The total weight of a liquid or gas
The number of particles in a volume of liquid or gas
The speed of particles in a solution
The temperature of a given material

questions.question: What does it mean when particles move 'down a concentration gradient'?
options: They move from lower concentration to higher concentration
They move from higher concentration to lower concentration
They move at a constant rate without changing position
They move only when energy is added to the system

questions.question: Why is diffusion defined as a 'passive' movement?
options: Because it requires extra energy from the cell
Because it happens naturally without requiring energy input
Because it only happens in living organisms
Because it only occurs when solutions are heated

questions.question: Which statement best defines diffusion?
options: The active transport of particles against a concentration gradient
The passive movement of particles from higher to lower concentration
The process of turning liquids into gases through heating
The movement of water molecules only across a fully impermeable barrier
